questions.question: Why do similar matrices $A$ and $P^{-1}AP$ have the same trace?
options: because $\operatorname{tr}(XY)=\operatorname{tr}(YX)$
because they have the same size
because trace ignores signs
because $P$ is invertible
questions.explanation: $\operatorname{tr}(P^{-1}AP)=\operatorname{tr}(APP^{-1})=\operatorname{tr}(A)$ by the cyclic property $\operatorname{tr}(XY)=\operatorname{tr}(YX)$.
questions.source_support: Cyclic property $\Rightarrow$ similarity-invariance.
questions.rewrite_notes: Hand-authored explanation + per-option explanations (why each wrong option is wrong + the likely misread).
option_explanations: Having the same size does not by itself give equal traces.
It is the cyclic property, not 'ignoring signs', that matters.
Invertibility of $P$ is used, but the key fact is $\operatorname{tr}(XY)=\operatorname{tr}(YX)$.

questions.question: Is $\operatorname{tr}(AB)=\operatorname{tr}(A)\,\operatorname{tr}(B)$ in general?
options: Yes, for diagonal matrices
No, it generally fails
Yes, for all square matrices
Yes, whenever $A,B$ commute
questions.explanation: In general $\operatorname{tr}(AB)\neq\operatorname{tr}(A)\operatorname{tr}(B)$; trace is additive, not multiplicative.
questions.source_support: Trace is additive, not multiplicative.
questions.rewrite_notes: Hand-authored explanation + per-option explanations (why each wrong option is wrong + the likely misread).
option_explanations: Even for diagonal matrices it fails: $\operatorname{diag}(1,1)$ gives $\operatorname{tr}(AB)=2$ but $\operatorname{tr}(A)\operatorname{tr}(B)=4$.

Take $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&0\end{pmatrix}$ and $B=\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix}$, both square: $AB=0$ so $\operatorname{tr}(AB)=0$, yet $\operatorname{tr}(A)\,\operatorname{tr}(B)=1\cdot1=1$; trace is additive, $\operatorname{tr}(AB)=\operatorname{tr}(BA)$, not multiplicative.
It fails even when $A,B$ commute.

questions.question: For matrices with both $AB$ and $BA$ defined, which always holds even when $AB\neq BA$?

$\operatorname{tr}(AB)=\operatorname{tr}(BA)$
$AB=BA$
questions.explanation: By the cyclic property of trace, $\operatorname{tr}(AB)=\operatorname{tr}(BA)$ always holds (when both products are defined), even when $AB\ne BA$.

questions.question: How are trace and determinant linked to eigenvalues?
options: Trace is the product of eigenvalues; determinant is their sum.
Trace is the sum of eigenvalues; determinant is their product.
Neither is related to eigenvalues.
Both are the largest eigenvalue.
questions.explanation: For a square matrix, the trace equals the sum of the eigenvalues (with algebraic multiplicity) and the determinant equals their product: $\operatorname{tr}(A)=\sum\lambda_i$ and $\det(A)=\prod\lambda_i$.
